milestone: R4 — motion quality and sustained operation
objective: Two questions one run answers: does motion look smooth or choppy at 8.5 fps, and does the device hold up over a minute of continuous full-colour streaming? A black 2x2 box travels a circle over a 253-colour sweep, sixteen laps, about 60 seconds.

target.pairing_precheck: authenticated exact target required before any socket is created

transport.one_controller_rule: the Android app must be disconnected for the whole run

operation.shape: one connection; 512 frames stepping a 2x2 box around a circle in 32 positions, repeated 16 times; per frame send preamble A, preamble B, image with 10 ms between packets, read one ACK, wait 50 ms; then close
operation.semantic_evidence: OPENDITOO-R3-FULLCOLOUR-THROUGHPUT-001 PASS at identical timing and comparable frame size: 118.2 ms per 1054-byte frame, 8.46 fps, 30/30 packets, 10/10 ACKs, zero errors, correct full-colour rendering confirmed by the operator. This extends duration and content, not timing.

source_frames.why: 32 positions of a black 2x2 box on a static 253-colour hue sweep, one circle of radius 5 about the centre, so the box advances roughly one pixel per frame. Each position is a distinct frozen image with its own hashes; the run repeats the loop 16 times. Distinctness is verified: 32 unique packet hashes.

measurements_required: achieved inter-frame interval over 512 frames, and whether it DRIFTS across the minute
per-frame ACK latency distribution and any upward trend
any frame whose ACK did not arrive, or any malformed ACK
total wall clock against the 60 s prediction
operator observation: is the motion smooth or choppy, and does it stay that way for the whole minute?
operator observation: does the unit feel warm, stall, flicker or behave oddly at any point?

budgets.derivation: 512 frames at R3's measured 118.2 ms is about 60.5 s. Wall clock is 120 s, roughly double, so a run that slows under sustained load is MEASURED rather than truncated -- drift is one of the two things this experiment exists to detect. Bytes are 512 x 1048.

expected_observations.transport: one connection, 1536 application packets, 512 wrapped 0x44 ACKs, clean local close after about 60 s
expected_observations.physical: a black square travelling smoothly clockwise in a circle over a rainbow sweep, sixteen laps in about a minute
expected_observations.what_would_be_a_finding: interval drifting upward, ACK latency climbing, the box stuttering or tearing, or the unit warming noticeably. Any of these is a real result about sustained streaming and is the point of running it.

persistence_analysis.basis: M6.4 power cycle returned the unit to stock software and the default clock
persistence_analysis.not_claimed: absence of any non-volatile write; repetition does not test that either
persistence_analysis.new_persistence_risk_vs_step_1: none identified: identical command, identical packets, same session shape, repeated. No new command id, no save/publish/upload, no gallery interaction.
persistence_analysis.new_risk_vs_previous: Frame SIZE is new; the command, packet structure, target, rate and session shape are unchanged. No new command id, no save/publish/upload, no gallery interaction. The encoder's 255-colour ceiling and the existing frame-size guard both still apply.

stop_immediately_on: unexpected target identity or pairing precheck failure
any ACK that is not exactly one 10-byte wrapped 0x44 frame
any send that does not complete in full
any conflicting controller observed on the link
a stock page takeover or any device behaviour outside the expected observations
stop_policy.on_ambiguous_outcome: stop, preserve the Host diagnostics record including the per-frame timings collected so far, and report. Do NOT resend, do not reconnect, do not power-cycle before the result is recorded.
stop_policy.recovery: operator-initiated only, after the outcome is recorded
stop_policy.operator_abort: the run is short enough to watch end to end; if it looks wrong, power off the Ditoo rather than letting it continue.

implementation_gate.status: built, installed and verified 2026-09-09. Installed DLL 7b921ece00250058ac3eb2b01c693b95ca96a1a28402346b994c54cd30f8592b, byte-identical to the repository build, REFRESH_STATUS=PASS_TYPED_IMAGE, OPENTIVOO_TASK=preserved, installed binary passes the shared receive fixture.
implementation_gate.boundary: The cap tracks the largest reviewed manifest and a test asserts it equals what some manifest in experiments/ actually requests, so it cannot drift upward on its own.

authority.grant_scope_requested: ONE execution: 512 frames, 1536 packets, 536576 application bytes, about 60 seconds of continuous transmission, 50 ms delay, 10 ms spacing, one connection, no retry, no reconnect. Not continuous or unattended display, not a higher rate.

explicitly_out_of_scope: any timing change; spacing and delay are held at R3's measured values
pipelining or any change to the one-ACK-per-frame shape
runs longer than 512 frames, or keeping the connection open beyond this run
any new command id, delta-frame or partial-update command, or command enumeration
driving frames from the M9 activity collector
why_this_value_matters: Every other timing number in this project was chosen by us and has proven reducible: the inter-frame delay went 1000 -> 250 -> 50 ms with no ill effect. The 40 ms send spacing is the ONLY timing taken from observed stock-app behaviour, so it is the only one that might encode a real device requirement.
why_this_shape: The operator's point: alternating full-screen images cannot show smoothness. A small object with continuous motion can -- a 2x2 box moving roughly one pixel per frame around a circle makes choppiness immediately obvious, and a black box on a rainbow sweep is maximally legible. Content stays at the 255-colour ceiling (1033 B images) so this remains a full-colour streaming test rather than a cheap one.

what_changes_and_what_does_not.changed: frame count 10 -> 512, duration ~1.2 s -> ~60 s, and content from A/B alternation to a 32-position motion loop. These move together because the questions -- smoothness and endurance -- are inherently multi-frame and multi-second.
what_changes_and_what_does_not.held_constant: timing is exactly R3's: 10 ms send spacing, 50 ms inter-frame delay. Same command, same packet structure, same target, same connection shape, same stop policy, same encoder, same 255-colour ceiling. The rate is already measured; this is not a rate experiment.
what_changes_and_what_does_not.why_that_is_acceptable: R1-R3 were rate measurements and each changed exactly one variable. This is a durability and perceptual qualification, where holding duration to one frame would defeat the purpose. Timing is the variable that must not move, and it does not.

the_real_risk.exposure: This is a large step in exposure: the longest transmission this project has ever performed is 10 frames in 1.2 s. This is 512 frames and 537 KB over about a minute, roughly 50x the frames and 500x the bytes of anything attempted before.
unknowns: whether the device throttles, heats or degrades under sustained load
whether the interval drifts upward across a minute, which ten-frame runs cannot show
whether the link stays stable far longer than it has ever been held
whether any resource grows unbounded on the Host across 512 operations
the_real_risk.why_it_is_still_bounded: Any malformed or missing ACK, any incomplete send, any ACK timeout or the wall-clock ceiling stops the run immediately with no retry and no reconnect. The failure mode is a stopped experiment, not an unbounded one. It remains supervised throughout.
the_real_risk.operator_abort: 60 seconds is long enough that watching matters. If the display looks wrong, stalls or the unit behaves oddly, power it off rather than letting the run finish; a stopped run is a recorded result, and the manifest is consumed either way.
